notes: Built from official program sources fetched 2026-10-09. 'name' is the IPEDS (HD2024) institution name when a confident match was found; 'listedAs' is the name the program itself uses. 'ipedsId' is the IPEDS UNITID. 'parentIpedsId' marks a branch campus that IPEDS reports under a parent institution, so don't treat it as the parent. eligibleResidentStates on an institution: null means every resident state the program lists (minus the school's own state); an array means the school restricts further. 'eligibleResidentCounties' (border agreements only) limits eligibility to the listed counties of that state. 'programs' (NEBHE, ACM) lists the approved majors and which home states each is open to.

programs.name: Western Undergraduate Exchange
sources: https://www.wiche.edu/tuition-savings/wue/wue-savings-finder/school-details/?schoolID={id} (one profile per institution; see each institution's sourceUrl)
programs.terms: Participating public two- and four-year colleges charge eligible out-of-state students no more than 150% of the school's in-state tuition, and some charge less (a few charge in-state rates). Private colleges don't participate. WUE isn't automatic: many schools cap awards, set GPA/test minimums, or exclude certain majors.
programs.howToGet: Apply to the school by its WUE deadline and ask for WUE on the application. Some schools award it automatically on admission; others need a separate WUE form, a minimum GPA, or an eligible major. Request it early, because many schools limit the number of awards.
programs.coverageNote: 169 participating institutions from WICHE's WUE Savings Finder dataset (embedded on the Savings Finder page), cross-checked against WICHE's 'WUE: List of Schools' page (168 names; the only differences are spelling variants). Eligible residents: 15 states plus American Samoa, CNMI, and Guam (WICHE 'For Students' page). Per-school restrictions are summarized from each school's Savings Finder profile, which the schools themselves maintain. estimatedTuition is WICHE's AY2025-26 tuition-only figure.

programs.terms: Minnesota and Wisconsin residents attending public colleges and universities in the other state are treated as residents for admission and tuition. Under the agreement they pay the higher of the two states' resident tuition rates at a comparable institution, which is usually Minnesota's rate. Professional programs (MD, DDS, DVM) are excluded.
programs.howToGet: Minnesota residents apply through the Minnesota Office of Higher Education; Wisconsin residents use the Universities of Wisconsin online reciprocity application (for Fall 2027, it opens February 1, 2027). This is separate from applying for admission. Wisconsin technical colleges: apply directly to the college.
